notes.summary: Spelling questions test whether you know the exact letters of common and tricky English words. SSC asks 1 to 2 in Tier 1 and more in Tier 2: find the misspelt word among four, pick the right spelling of one word, or spot and correct a misspelt word in a sentence. A few rules (ie/ei, doubling, silent e, -able/-ible, -ance/-ence) and a list of about 150 trouble words cover most questions. SSC follows British spelling (colour, travelled, programme).

concepts.title: How SSC asks spelling questions
concepts.body:
• Find the misspelt word: four different words, one is wrong (Edible / Delegait / Rebel / Monarch). The most common form.
  • Choose the correct spelling: four versions of one word (propotion / proportion / preportion / proporsion).
  • In a sentence: find the misspelt word, or choose the correct form of the underlined word (accomodate → accommodate). Sometimes No error is an option.
  • Fill the blank with the correctly spelt word, or pick the spelling of a word with a given meaning.
  • Error-free sentence: four sentences, choose the one with no spelling mistake.

concepts.title: A quick checking method
concepts.body:
1. Say the word slowly in syllables: ac-com-mo-date, en-vi-ron-ment.
  2. Check the usual danger spots: double letters, ie / ei, vowel in the ending (-ance/-ence, -able/-ible), silent letters.
  3. In find the misspelt word questions, the wrong word often has a letter swapped (Evolutoin), dropped (Overide), doubled (Dillemma) or replaced by its sound (Visious, Gingar).
  4. Trust a spelling only when you are sure; otherwise eliminate the ones you know are right.

concepts.title: ie or ei
concepts.body:
i before e, except after c, when the sound is ee.
PatternExamples
ie (sound ee)believe, achieve, field, piece, siege, relieve, grief
ei after creceive, deceive, ceiling, conceive, receipt
ei with sound ayneighbour, weigh, eight, vein, reign
Exceptions to learnweird, seize, either, neither, leisure, protein, foreign, height, their, forfeit
ie after c (c sounds sh)ancient, efficient, sufficient, conscience, species, science

concepts.title: Doubling the final consonant
concepts.body:
• One-syllable word, one vowel + one consonant: double before a vowel suffix. stop → stopped, run → running, big → bigger.
  • Longer word stressed on the last syllable: double. begin → beginning, occur → occurred, occurrence, refer → referred, admit → admitted, commit → committed.
  • Stress on an earlier syllable: do not double. visit → visited, offer → offered, benefit → benefited, develop → developed, refer → reference (stress moves).
  • British English doubles a final l after one vowel: travel → travelled, cancel → cancelled, label → labelled, counsel → counsellor.
  • Never double w, x or y: fixed, showing, played.

concepts.title: Silent e and final y
concepts.body:
• Drop the silent e before a vowel suffix: hope → hoping, write → writing, desire → desirable, argue → arguing.
  • Keep the e before a consonant suffix: hopeful, movement, careful, excitement. Exceptions: argument, truly, ninth, wholly, awful.
  • Keep the e after soft c or g before -able / -ous: noticeable, manageable, courageous, outrageous.
  • Consonant + y changes to i: happy → happiness, carry → carried, beauty → beautiful, but keep y before -ing: carrying, studying.
  • Vowel + y keeps the y: play → played, enjoy → enjoyment. Exceptions: paid, said, laid.

concepts.title: Endings that sound alike
concepts.body:
EndingWords to learn
-ance / -antappearance, maintenance, guidance, assistance, attendance, perseverance, relevant, tolerance
-ence / -entexistence, independence, occurrence, conscience, interference, reference, presence, permanent
-ableacceptable, dependable, noticeable, indispensable, available, inevitable
-iblevisible, possible, terrible, edible, eligible, responsible, flexible, irresistible
-cede / -ceed / -sedeonly supersede ends in -sede; only exceed, proceed, succeed end in -ceed; the rest end in -cede: precede, concede, recede, intercede
-ise / -izeboth accepted for most words (organise, organize); always -ise: advertise, supervise, compromise, exercise, surprise
-ary / -erydictionary, necessary, secretary, library; cemetery, stationery (paper), monastery
Rough guide: -able usually follows a complete word (accept-able); -ible usually follows a part that is not a word on its own (vis-ible).

concepts.body:

American spellings are not usually given as the wrong option, because both are real spellings. If both appear, prefer the British one.

varieties.name: Find the misspelt word
varieties.how: Check each word for the usual danger spots: double letters, ie/ei, endings and silent letters. Mark the ones you are sure are correct; the one left is the answer.

example.q:
Select the incorrectly spelt word.
Professional / Dillemma / Perpetuate / Electronics
steps: Professional: one f, double s. Correct.
Dilemma has one l and double m; Dillemma is wrong.

varieties.name: Choose the correct spelling
varieties.how: All four are versions of one word. Say it in syllables and compare the options letter by letter at the danger spot.

example.q:
Select the correctly spelt word.
Embarassment / Embarrasment / Embarrassment / Embaressment
steps: Rule: embarrass has double r and double s.
Only one option has both doubles and -ment.

varieties.name: Misspelt word in a sentence
varieties.how: Read the sentence slowly and check the long or unusual words first; short common words are rarely the error.

example.q:
Identify the incorrectly spelt word in the given sentence.
One part of the philosophy of life's meaning consists of the systemetic attempt to identify what people have in mind.
steps: Long words: philosophy, meaning, systemetic, attempt, identify.

varieties.name: Correct the misspelt word
varieties.how: Recall the correct form of the marked word and choose it. If the word is already right and No error is offered, choose that.

example.q:
Select the option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word.
I doubt that these lifts can accomodate 100 people.
steps: Rule: double c and double m.

varieties.name: Correctly spelt word for a blank
varieties.how: First decide which word the blank needs (watch sound-alikes like dew/due), then pick its correct spelling.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
_____ droplets settled on top of the leaves.
steps: Water drops on leaves in the morning = dew.
Options: Due, Doe, Do, Dew. The others sound alike but mean owed, a female deer and to perform.

varieties.name: Correct spelling of a word with a given meaning
varieties.how: Name the word from the meaning, then check the options for the right letters.

example.q: Select the correct spelling of a word meaning 'to make less severe or intense'.
steps: Options: Mitigate, Mittigate, Mitagagate, Mittagete. One t in the middle, -gate at the end.

varieties.name: Sentence with no spelling error
varieties.how: Scan each sentence for one doubtful word. Three sentences will each have one mistake; the fourth has none.

example.q: Select the sentence that contains no spelling errors.
steps: (a) The committee will recieve the report tomorrow. recieve → receive.
(b) Their behaviour was definately rude. definately → definitely.
(c) We need a seperate room. seperate → separate.
(d) The government will guarantee the loan. All correct.
example.answer: The government will guarantee the loan.

tips: Say the word in syllables before you judge it: en-vi-ron-ment, gov-ern-ment.
Check double letters first; they cause most SSC spelling errors.
Use the rules: i before e except after c; double the last consonant when the stress is on the last syllable.
Mark the words you are sure of; the odd one out is often the answer.
SSC follows British spelling: colour, centre, travelled, programme.
Revise 10 trouble words a day with the spelling flashcards and write them once by hand.
traps: A word can look right but be the wrong sound-alike (stationary for stationery).
Supersede is the only -sede word; exceed, proceed, succeed are the only -ceed words.
When No error is an option, check carefully before assuming a mistake.

questions.solution: The correct spelling is Achieve (i before e, no c before it). Receive and Deceive follow 'ei after c'.
The correct spelling is Liaison (l-i-a-i-s-o-n). The other three are correct.
